review.title: Flagship review task - explain the module and find the bugs
review.task: Read test/orders.js, explain briefly what the module does, and identify any bugs.
review.notes: Same fixture, same prompt and the same deterministic grader as claude-code-eco, so the two projects' quality columns are directly comparable even though their token counts are not.

trivial.title: Trivial question - does the mode volunteer an out-of-scope warning?
trivial.notes: The question never asks for a review; the crash bug sits in an adjacent function.

review-thread.title: Realistic thread - review, then fix, then harden (three turns, one thread)
review-thread.task: Read test/orders.js, explain briefly what the module does, and identify any bugs.
turns: Fix the crash you found. Do not change anything else.
What else in this module would you harden, and why?
review-thread.notes: Every earlier batch measured a single turn, which is the worst case for an always-on instruction block: the block is uncached on turn 1 and there is no later turn for its output savings to repeat over. Real usage is a thread, so this study resumes one thread across three turns and sums the usage. Turn 1 is identical to the `review` study and is what the rubric grades, so the quality column stays comparable; turns 2 and 3 add a patch and an open-ended question, which is where the no-recap, no-re-read and no-survey rules can act.
